title: You Got a Raise. So Why Aren't You Richer? (Tax Brackets)
alts: Tax Brackets Explained: Why a Raise Can't Make You Take Home Less
Your $5,000 Raise Is Really $2,000. Here's Where It Went.
line1: Got a raise but don't feel richer? Dave's $5,000 raise shrinks to ~$2,000 after taxes and inflation, then a car payment eats the rest.
summary: Dave gets a $5,000 raise and celebrates with a new car, then ends up with less money each month than before. We follow the raise: the tax bracket myth busted with buckets (2026 IRS brackets, only dollars above $50,400 of taxable income pay 22%), payroll taxes, inflation and real vs nominal wages (BLS: real average hourly earnings fell 0.3% in the year to August 2026 while typical raises were about 3.5%), lifestyle creep, the hedonic treadmill, and who profits when you upgrade, from record $777 car payments to 84-month loans (Edmunds). Then the fix: save half of every raise automatically.
